paper_title: FactBench A Dynamic Benchmark for In-the-Wild Language Model Factuality   Evaluation
caption: Distribution of LM's answer refusal categories on
model_annotation: The pie charts illustrate the distribution of answer refusal categories across four different language models—GPT4-o, Gemini1.5-Pro, Llama3.1-70B-Instruct, and Llama3.1-405B-Instruct—as evaluated on the FactBench benchmark. Each chart is divided into segments representing distinct refusal reasons, labeled with both the category name and its count and percentage. For GPT4-o, “Lack of Knowledge” dominates at 5 instances (83.3%), with “Safety” accounting for 1 (16.7%). Gemini1.5-Pro shows a more balanced distribution: “Misinformation” is largest at 33 (38.4%), followed by “Lack of Knowledge” (8, 22.1%), “Ethical Advice” (14, 16.3%), “Clarification” (12, 14.0%), and “Safety” (8, 9.3%). Llama3.1-70B-Instruct primarily refuses due to “Lack of Knowledge” (3, 75.0%), with “Clarification” making up the remaining 25.0% (1 instance). Llama3.1-405B-Instruct splits evenly between “Lack of Knowledge” and “Misinformation,” each at 2 instances (50.0%). The charts use distinct colors for each category and include percentage labels within each slice, with no legend provided. The visual emphasis is on the proportional contribution of each refusal type per model, with no apparent ordering beyond the largest segment typically placed at the top or right.
